ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Inspired by the Beijing Winter Olympics, a team of beginners underwent 3 months of alpine skiing intensive training, and their performance improved significantly, while body weight and oxygen uptake per unit time during skiing both showed no obvious change. The plasma lactate concentration of the trainees after completing skiing movements before and after intensive training was tested, and the results are shown in the figure below. Compared with before intensive training, what respiration of the trainees was enhanced per unit time during skiing?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Inspired by the Beijing Winter Olympics, a team of beginners underwent 3 months of alpine skiing intensive training, and their performance improved significantly, while body weight and oxygen uptake per unit time during skiing both showed no obvious change. The plasma lactate concentration of the trainees after completing skiing movements before and after intensive training was tested, and the results are shown in the figure below. Compared with before intensive training, what respiration of the trainees was enhanced per unit time during skiing?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a bar chart, with the vertical axis labeled “lactate concentration (mmol·L⁻¹)” and the horizontal axis comparing “before intensive training” and “after intensive training.” The bar height before intensive training is about 7 mmol·L⁻¹, and the bar height after intensive training is about 11 mmol·L⁻¹; after intensive training it is obviously higher than before intensive training, indicating that the plasma lactate concentration increased after completing skiing movements. Then reason: The stem states that body weight and oxygen uptake per unit time during skiing before and after training both showed no obvious change, so the oxygen uptake level related to aerobic respiration per unit time did not obviously increase. Lactate is a product of anaerobic respiration in animal cells. After training, lactate accumulation per unit time increased, indicating that anaerobic respiration per unit time of the trainees during skiing was enhanced.
